posts.title: The Abyss Regurgitated Me
posts.description: ← Back to Writing One of my own illustrations. A thin stream of bubbles escaped through the exhaust valve of my drysuit as I descended. I turned my wrist towards the beam of my light. 48 m. PO₂ stable at 1.2. 3 h 15 min left on the scrubber. Everything according to plan. My buddy was a few metres ahead of me. He turned, raised one hand and gave me the signal. All good. We stayed on the guideline. Then something tore through the water. A heavy vibration passed through my chest, my teeth, every bone inside me, and snapped my whole body sideways before I had time to react. It was violent and impossibly fast. "What was th —" A second, stronger vibration came before I had finished the thought. I blinked, and my buddy was gone. The sound arrived a fraction of a second later. A cracking roar so horribly loud that it felt as though something enormous had broken directly inside my skull. Where my buddy had been, there was now a wall. I reached out and touched it. posts.title: The Eye in The Deep
posts.description: ← Back to Writing One of my own illustrations : Portrait of Cornelius Hickey. Frame of “The Terror” In the middle of the ocean, in its depths, where no one has ever reached nor ever will, a round mark appeared. Formed by stones that had moved into unreadable symbols, with an eye at its center that opened, the earth began to tremble across the world. In that same moment, somewhere in the world, there was a ship moving slowly through a canal in a city. Sailors called it a Leviathan, a sea devil, one that doomed anyone who boarded. It almost sank once, causing thousands of deaths. One of the workers aboard was a survivor of a previous catastrophe. A proud man, now older, he felt a strange bond with this ship that brought nothing but misfortune. When he heard creaking, like something scraping along the hull, fear set in.
